Class TuiView

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.am02.client.view.AbstractClientView
it.polimi.ingsw.am02.client.view.tui.TuiView
All Implemented Interfaces:
ClientView
public class TuiView extends AbstractClientView
Text-based user interface for the MESOS game client.

Renders the complete game state to the terminal using ANSI escape codes. Handles both lobby and in-game phases.

Reconnection strategy

When a player reconnects, the GameController replays the full event history ("fast-forward"). Each event updates GameModel state incrementally. The view does not attempt to render during fast-forward because setGameModel(GameModel) has not been called yet (or gameModel is still being populated). As soon as the controller calls setGameModel(populatedModel), this view immediately performs a full repaint — showing cards, resources, and turn order exactly as they are.

Notification buffer

Only the last 10 log lines are kept; older ones are silently discarded.

Thread model

All public callbacks enqueue a Runnable onto eventQueue. A single background thread (TUI-Event-Processor) drains the queue sequentially, guaranteeing that terminal writes never interleave.

  • Method Details

    • setGameModel

      public void setGameModel(GameModel gameModel)
      Binds the populated game model and immediately forces a full repaint.

      This is the single hook that makes reconnection work: the controller calls this method after the fast-forward event sequence has fully updated the model. The first render therefore always reflects the complete, current game state — cards taken, resources, turn order, etc.

      Specified by:
      setGameModel in interface ClientView
      Overrides:
      setGameModel in class AbstractClientView
      Parameters:
      gameModel - the populated client-side game model; null resets the view to the pre-game state
